# Fiscal Re-Acceleration

Report 187 | Published 2026-04-25 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2026-4-25/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/187.json)

Fiscal momentum, bank resilience and DeFi risk.

The fiscal reacceleration call has a measurable success, and the FIMA explanation correctly identifies a funding backstop. The jet-fuel denominator is wrong. DeFi emergency control validates a centralization concern, while Lido’s falling market share challenges a simple winner-take-all story. Bank results are constructive but mixed across securities.

**Coverage:** Full numbered text and image inventory read. All material theses across macro, digital assets, investment analysis and concluding sections considered. Position listings and incidental descriptive statistics are excluded unless they support a thesis.

The standard all-chain DefiLlama series supports the comparison. Excluding liquid staking and double-counted TVL, the 2021 maximum was $177.46bn on November 9; the highest subsequent observation through April 26, 2026 was $167.91bn on October 7, 2025. Publication-day TVL was $81.10bn. This is dollar-denominated collateral value, so it does not by itself measure users, real activity or investment returns.

**Direction:** Historical dollar TVL remained below its 2021 peak under the standard endpoint definition.

**Timing:** Tested through the April 26, 2026 publication date.

**Mechanism:** Token prices and collateral composition influence TVL; the series does not establish technology adoption or causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium
